metadata.title: Cyclophosphamide (IV), Methotrexate and 5-Fluorouracil (CMF) – 28 day
metadata.indication: Adjuvant breast carcinoma when unsuitable for anthracyclines, or metastatic breast carcinoma.
metadata.partial_assessment_policy: Each entered value is assessed independently. Omitted domains remain unassessed and are never assumed normal.

catalogue_reconciliation.scope_note: The NCCP states that its website list is not comprehensive. This reconciliation does not assert that every possible national regimen is published online.

encoding_maturity.label: Source reconciled encoding · independent clinical and pharmacy review pending
encoding_maturity.scope_note: Individual CMF route/schedule, renal tables, count gaps and source omissions reviewed. No independent clinical validation or authorisation.

metadata.schedule_summary: Fluorouracil 600 mg/m², methotrexate 40 mg/m² and cyclophosphamide 600 mg/m² IV on Days 1 and 8 every 28 days. Adjuvant: 6 cycles; metastatic: until progression or unacceptable toxicity.
source_boundaries: ANC 1.49–1.5 and platelets 89–90 are not assigned by the printed strict/integer bands.
The count table uses OR, including its full-dose row; discordant counts must not permit automatic clearance.
Methotrexate CrCl exactly 50 overlaps the ≥50 and 20–50 rows.
IV cyclophosphamide CrCl >29 to 30 is unassigned by the 10–29 and >30 rows.
The IV28 5-FU hepatic row does not state a severe-impairment recommendation.

clinical_governance.prescriptive_authority: Treatment plan must be initiated by a Consultant Medical Oncologist.
clinical_governance.dose_modification_note: Any dose modification should be discussed with a Consultant.
clinical_governance.disclaimer: Decision-support encoding of the current NCCP source. It does not replace the official regimen, clinical judgement, local policy, prescribing review, or pharmacy verification.

rules.explanation: Complete DPD deficiency: do not administer fluorouracil. Agree an alternative regimen.

action.recommendation: Partial DPD deficiency: consider a reduced fluorouracil starting dose. This source does not specify a universal percentage; later escalation requires absence of serious toxicity, careful monitoring and prescriber review.

action.recommendation: CrCl below 20 mL/min: methotrexate is not recommended. If unavoidable, seek specialist advice including consideration of haemodialysis; no automatic methotrexate dose.

rules.explanation: CrCl below 20 mL/min: methotrexate is not recommended. If unavoidable, seek specialist advice including consideration of haemodialysis; no automatic methotrexate dose.

action.recommendation: CrCl 20 to below 50 mL/min: source lists 50% of the original methotrexate dose. Confirm other component actions and consultant-approved prescription.

rules.explanation: CrCl 20 to below 50 mL/min: source lists 50% of the original methotrexate dose. Confirm other component actions and consultant-approved prescription.

action.recommendation: Bilirubin above 86 µmol/L: avoid methotrexate.

rules.explanation: Bilirubin above 86 µmol/L: avoid methotrexate.

action.recommendation: Methotrexate is not recommended during haemodialysis; if unavoidable the source lists 50% original dose and daily high-flux dialysis under specialist care. 5-FU generally needs no dialysis-related adjustment. IV cyclophosphamide is not recommended; if unavoidable consider 50% original dose.

rules.explanation: Methotrexate is not recommended during haemodialysis; if unavoidable the source lists 50% original dose and daily high-flux dialysis under specialist care. 5-FU generally needs no dialysis-related adjustment. IV cyclophosphamide is not recommended; if unavoidable consider 50% original dose.

action.recommendation: CrCl below 10 mL/min: IV cyclophosphamide is not recommended; if unavoidable consider 50% of the original dose following consultant/pharmacy review.

action.recommendation: CrCl 10–29 mL/min: consider IV cyclophosphamide at 75% of the original dose. This is a clinical choice, not an automatic reduction.

action.recommendation: The 5-FU hepatic no-adjustment statement is qualified by absence of renal impairment. Combined renal/hepatic dysfunction requires specialist review rather than an assumed full dose.

rules.explanation: The 5-FU hepatic no-adjustment statement is qualified by absence of renal impairment. Combined renal/hepatic dysfunction requires specialist review rather than an assumed full dose.

action.recommendation: Pleural effusion or ascites may retain methotrexate and prolong exposure. Review third-space fluid and the methotrexate plan before dosing; no fixed reduction is specified.

rules.explanation: Pleural effusion or ascites may retain methotrexate and prolong exposure. Review third-space fluid and the methotrexate plan before dosing; no fixed reduction is specified.

action.recommendation: Withhold fluorouracil and urgently assess new chest pain/ischaemic or other significant cardiac symptoms before further treatment. 5-FU cardiotoxicity requires clinical investigation; this source does not provide a numerical rechallenge algorithm.

action.recommendation: Suspected current febrile neutropenia requires urgent clinical assessment and treatment withholding. Do not translate it into an unsupported future-cycle percentage reduction.

supportive_care.supportive_medications_label: NCCP antiemetic guidance for moderate emetogenic risk
supportive_care.mapping_basis: IV cyclophosphamide 600 mg/m² is moderate risk; 5-FU and methotrexate are low risk. Repeat prescribed prevention on each actual administration day.
regimen_specific_notes: No routine hypersensitivity premedication is usually required; this does not remove the need for antiemetics.
Anti-diarrhoeal treatment follows local policy; provide escalation instructions.
Hydration must be individualised. NCCP suggests 2–3 L on Days 1 and 8; confirm this against the actual treatment schedule and cardiac/renal restrictions.
Review pleural effusion/ascites, DPD testing and 5-FU cardiac symptoms.
